people.name: Panini
people.summary: Sanskrit grammarian from Gandhara (Shalatula, near Attock) who wrote the Ashtadhyayi, about 4,000 rules of Sanskrit grammar.
facts: Ashtadhyayi ("eight chapters").
Patanjali later wrote the Mahabhashya on it.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Bharata Muni
people.summary: Author of the Natyashastra, the ancient Sanskrit treatise on drama, dance and music; source of the rasa theory.
facts: Described eight rasas (a ninth, shanta, was added later).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Charaka
people.summary: Physician of the Kushana age (by tradition, at Kanishka's court) whose Charaka Samhita is the basic text of Ayurveda.
facts: Charaka Samhita on internal medicine.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Sushruta
people.summary: Ancient surgeon whose Sushruta Samhita describes many surgical instruments and operations, including plastic surgery of the nose.
facts: Called the father of Indian surgery.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Varahamihira
people.summary: Astronomer of Ujjain who wrote the Panchasiddhantika and the encyclopaedic Brihatsamhita.
facts: Panchasiddhantika summarised five astronomical systems.
By tradition one of the nine gems of a Vikramaditya.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Brahmagupta
people.summary: Mathematician who wrote the Brahmasphutasiddhanta (628 CE), with rules for zero and negative numbers.
facts: First to give rules for arithmetic with zero.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ilango Adigal
people.summary: Chera prince and Jaina monk, by tradition, who wrote the Tamil epic Silappadikaram (the story of Kannagi and Kovalan).
facts: Silappadikaram ("the tale of the anklet").
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Vishnu Sharma
people.summary: Author of the Panchatantra, animal fables for teaching princes statecraft, translated into many languages.
facts: Translated into Pahlavi and Arabic (Kalila wa Dimna).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Dhananjaya
people.summary: Renati Chola king whose Kalamalla inscription (Kadapa district, c. 575 CE) is the earliest known inscription fully in Telugu.
facts: The Renati Cholas ruled Renadu (Kadapa–Kurnool).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Narasimhavarman II
people.summary: Pallava king (Rajasimha) who built the Shore Temple at Mamallapuram and the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram.
facts: Structural (built, not rock-cut) temples began under him.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Pampa
people.summary: Adikavi of Kannada, born at Vemulavada (Telangana), who wrote Vikramarjuna Vijaya (941) and Adipurana at the Vemulavada Chalukya court.
facts: One of the "three gems" of Kannada with Ponna and Ranna.
His brother Jinavallabha's Kurkyala inscription has early Telugu verse.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kalhana
people.summary: Kashmiri poet-historian who wrote the Rajatarangini (1148), the first true historical chronicle in Sanskrit.
facts: Covers Kashmir's kings in eight books (tarangas).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Jayadeva
people.summary: Sanskrit poet of Odisha/Bengal who wrote the Gita Govinda (12th century) on Radha and Krishna.
facts: Court poet, by tradition, of Lakshmana Sena of Bengal.
Gita Govinda songs are sung at Puri.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Vishnuvardhana (Hoysala)
people.summary: Hoysala king who built the Chennakeshava temple at Belur (1117) after a victory; converted from Jainism to Vaishnavism under Ramanuja.
facts: His queen Shantala Devi was a famous dancer.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Anantavarman Chodaganga
people.summary: Eastern Ganga king of Kalinga (1078–1147) who built the Jagannath temple at Puri; his empire ran from the Ganga to the Godavari.
facts: Son of an Eastern Ganga king and a Chola princess.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Narasimhadeva I
people.summary: Eastern Ganga king who built the Sun Temple at Konark (c. 1250) and fought the Bengal sultans.
facts: Konark is shaped as a chariot with 24 wheels and 7 horses.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Palkuriki Somanatha
people.summary: Virashaiva Telugu poet who wrote the Basava Puranam and Panditaradhya Charitra in the "desi" style, using common people's Telugu (12th–13th century).
facts: First to use the dwipada metre for a long work.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Muinuddin Chishti
people.summary: Sufi saint who came to India in 1192 and settled at Ajmer, founding the Chishti order in India; his dargah is visited by people of all faiths (NCERT).
facts: Called "Gharib Nawaz" (comforter of the poor).
Akbar walked to his dargah 14 times (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 6 "Bhakti-Sufi Traditions"

people.name: Madhvacharya
people.summary: Philosopher from Udupi who taught Dvaita (dualism) — God and the soul are always separate.
facts: Founded the Krishna matha at Udupi.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Jnaneshwar
people.summary: Marathi saint-poet who wrote the Jnaneshwari (1290), a commentary on the Gita in Marathi; a founder of the Warkari tradition of Pandharpur (NCERT).
facts: Namdev, Eknath and Tukaram followed (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Gona Budda Reddy
people.summary: Telugu poet of the Kakatiya age who wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam in dwipada, the first Telugu Ramayana.
facts: Kakatiya feudatory of Vardhamanapuram.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
people.summary: Bhakti saint of Bengal who spread devotion to Krishna through kirtan (group singing); settled at Puri.
facts: Founder of Gaudiya Vaishnavism.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Purandara Dasa
people.summary: Kannada saint-composer of Vijayanagara called the "father of Carnatic music"; organised its basic lessons.
facts: Disciple of Vyasatirtha.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Music and dance on stamps / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Mirabai
people.summary: Rajput princess of Merta, married into the Sisodia family of Mewar, who became a devotee of Krishna and a disciple of Ravidas (NCERT).
facts: Her bhajans challenged the norms of the upper castes (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Atukuri Molla
people.summary: Telugu poet from a potter family (Gopavaram, Kadapa) who wrote a simple Molla Ramayanam (16th century).
facts: One of the first women poets of Telugu.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Tulsidas
people.summary: Hindi poet who wrote the Ramcharitmanas (begun 1574) in Awadhi (NCERT).
facts: Also wrote the Hanuman Chalisa (by tradition).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Surdas
people.summary: Blind poet of Braj who wrote the Sursagar on Krishna (NCERT).
facts: Disciple of Vallabhacharya.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Vemana
people.summary: Telugu "praja kavi" (people's poet) whose short verses ending "Vishwadabhirama vinura vema" attack caste and ritual; C.P. Brown collected and translated them (1829).
facts: Born in Rayalaseema, by tradition.
Dates uncertain — often placed in the 17th century.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kshetrayya
people.summary: Telugu composer of padams (love songs to Muvva Gopala) for dance, at the courts of the Nayaks of Madurai and Tanjore and Golconda (17th century).
facts: From Muvva (Movva), Krishna district.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Tarigonda Vengamamba
people.summary: Telugu poet and devotee of Venkateswara who started free food (annadanam) at Tirumala.
facts: Wrote Venkatachala Mahatmyam.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Siddhendra Yogi
people.summary: Founder of Kuchipudi dance-drama who wrote Bhama Kalapam and taught it to the boys of Kuchipudi village (17th century, by tradition).
facts: Founder of Kuchipudi dance-drama who wrote Bhama Kalapam and taught it to the boys of Kuchipudi village (17th century, by tradition).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ustad Ahmad Lahori
people.summary: Architect regarded as the chief designer of the Taj Mahal and of the Red Fort in Delhi.
facts: Architect regarded as the chief designer of the Taj Mahal and of the Red Fort in Delhi.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Tyagaraja
people.summary: Telugu saint-composer of Tiruvaiyaru, greatest of the Trinity of Carnatic music, who wrote thousands of kritis on Rama.
facts: Pancharatna kritis.
His forefathers came from Kakarla, Prakasam district.
Trinity: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Colin Mackenzie
people.summary: First Surveyor General of India who surveyed Hampi (1800) and collected thousands of local histories (kaifiyats), inscriptions and manuscripts of south India, largely through his Telugu assistants, the Kavali brothers.
facts: Mackenzie manuscripts are now in the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, Chennai.
The syllabus names him with C.P. Brown and Thomas Munro.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: C.P. Brown
people.summary: Company official who revived Telugu literature: collected and printed old works, published Vemana's verses in English (1829) and wrote a Telugu–English dictionary (1852).
facts: Served at Kadapa, Machilipatnam and Rajahmundry.
Set up free schools and paid pandits to copy manuscripts.
Wrote a Telugu grammar (1840) and dictionaries.
The C.P. Brown Library at Kadapa honours him.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Raja Ravi Varma
people.summary: Painter from Travancore who combined European oil technique with Indian themes; his prints of gods and heroines reached every home.
facts: Set up a printing press at Lonavala (1894).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu
people.summary: Brahmo Samaj leader of Andhra who led the social purity (anti-nautch) movement and worked against untouchability; principal of Pithapuram Raja's College, Kakinada.
facts: Vice-Chancellor of Madras University (1925).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Gidugu Ramamurthy
people.summary: Linguist of Parlakimidi who led the movement for spoken Telugu (vyavaharika bhasha) in writing and teaching, and created a script and books for the Savara tribal language.
facts: His birthday, 29 August, is Telugu Language Day.
Fought the "grandhika" (classical) Telugu purists.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
people.summary: Journalist of Kurnool, among the first Andhras jailed for sedition (1908), and a leader of the library movement.
facts: Edited Swarajya; jailed in 1908.
First president of the Andhra Desa Grandhalaya Sangham, with Ayyanki.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ayyanki Venkataramanaiah
people.summary: Father of the library movement in Andhra; founded the Andhra Desa Grandhalaya Sangham at Vijayawada (1914) and the journal Grandhalaya Sarvasvamu.
facts: Called "Grandhalaya Pitamaha".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Mutnuri Krishna Rao
people.summary: Editor of the Krishna Patrika (Machilipatnam) for nearly four decades, a voice of nationalism in Andhra.
facts: Krishna Patrika began in 1902.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ponaka Kanakamma
people.summary: Nellore social worker and freedom fighter who founded the Sujanaranjani Samajam (1913) and the Kasturba Devi girls' school, and was jailed in the Salt Satyagraha.
facts: Nellore social worker and freedom fighter who founded the Sujanaranjani Samajam (1913) and the Kasturba Devi girls' school, and was jailed in the Salt Satyagraha.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Dokka Seethamma
people.summary: Woman of Lankala Gannavaram (Konaseema) famous for feeding every hungry traveller; called "Apara Annapurna".
facts: Edward VII honoured her picture at his coronation, by tradition.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: T.M. Nair
people.summary: Doctor and co-founder of the Justice Party (South Indian Liberal Federation, 1916) with Theagaraya Chetty.
facts: Doctor and co-founder of the Justice Party (South Indian Liberal Federation, 1916) with Theagaraya Chetty.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Theagaraya Chetty
people.summary: Co-founder of the Justice Party (1916) who issued the "Non-Brahmin Manifesto".
facts: Co-founder of the Justice Party (1916) who issued the "Non-Brahmin Manifesto".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Raja of Panagal
people.summary: Telugu Justice Party leader, Chief Minister (Premier) of Madras Presidency (1921–26), who issued the first Communal G.O. on job reservation (1921) and set up Andhra University (1926).
facts: Passed the Hindu Religious Endowments Act (1925).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: K. S. Muthiah & Co., Madras / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Narayana Guru
people.summary: Kerala reformer of the Ezhava community who consecrated a Shiva idol at Aruvippuram (1888) and gave the message "one caste, one religion, one God for man"; the SNDP Yogam (1903) spread his work.
facts: Kerala reformer of the Ezhava community who consecrated a Shiva idol at Aruvippuram (1888) and gave the message "one caste, one religion, one God for man"; the SNDP Yogam (1903) spread his work.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Rayaprolu Subbarao
people.summary: Telugu poet who began "bhava kavitvam" (romantic poetry) with Trinakankanam (1913) and wrote the patriotic "Ye desamegina endu kalidina".
facts: Called "Abhinava Nannaya".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Garimella Satyanarayana
people.summary: Poet of Srikakulam whose song "Maa kodi tella doratanamu" (we don't want white rule) (1921) became the anthem of Non-Cooperation in Andhra; he was jailed for it.
facts: Poet of Srikakulam whose song "Maa kodi tella doratanamu" (we don't want white rule) (1921) became the anthem of Non-Cooperation in Andhra; he was jailed for it.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Unnava Lakshminarayana
people.summary: Lawyer and reformer of Guntur who wrote Malapalli (1922), a novel on Dalit and peasant life that the British banned; led the Palnadu forest satyagraha.
facts: Founded a widows' home at Guntur.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary
people.summary: Rationalist poet and lawyer of Krishna district ("Kaviraju") who attacked caste and Brahmin priestly privilege in Sambuka Vadha and Kurukshetra Sangramamu.
facts: Known as "Kaviraju".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Gurram Jashuva
people.summary: Dalit Telugu poet of Vinukonda whose Gabbilam (the bat, 1941) carries a Dalit's message to Shiva, since he may not enter the temple; Sahitya Akademi Award 1964 for Kreestu Charitra.
facts: Also wrote Firdausi and Kandiseekudu.
Padma Bhushan 1970.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Boyi Bheemanna
people.summary: Dalit Telugu poet and playwright of Konaseema whose play Palerugadu (1940s) and long poem Gudiselu Kalipotunnai (Sahitya Akademi 1975) spoke for the oppressed.
facts: Padma Bhushan 2001.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Sri Sri
people.summary: Srirangam Srinivasa Rao, revolutionary poet of Visakhapatnam whose Maha Prasthanam (poems from 1934, published 1950) began progressive Telugu poetry; led the Viplava Rachayitala Sangham (1970).
facts: Srirangam Srinivasa Rao, revolutionary poet of Visakhapatnam whose Maha Prasthanam (poems from 1934, published 1950) began progressive Telugu poetry; led the Viplava Rachayitala Sangham (1970).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Shaik Nazar
people.summary: Burrakatha artist of Ponnekallu (Guntur) who made the folk ballad form a tool of the Praja Natya Mandali and the people's movements.
facts: Padma Shri 1986.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Dadasaheb Phalke
people.summary: Maker of India's first full-length feature film, Raja Harishchandra (1913); the highest film award is named after him (1969).
facts: Maker of India's first full-length feature film, Raja Harishchandra (1913); the highest film award is named after him (1969).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: H.M. Reddy
people.summary: Director of Bhakta Prahlada (1931), the first Telugu talkie.
facts: Director of Bhakta Prahlada (1931), the first Telugu talkie.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Viswanatha Satyanarayana
people.summary: Telugu poet-novelist, "Kavi Samrat", who won the first Jnanpith for Telugu (1970) for Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu; also wrote Veyipadagalu.
facts: Veyipadagalu was translated into Hindi by P.V. Narasimha Rao (Sahasraphan).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: C. Narayana Reddy
people.summary: Telugu poet and film lyricist who won the Jnanpith (1988) for Viswambhara.
facts: Telugu poet and film lyricist who won the Jnanpith (1988) for Viswambhara.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: The original uploader was Yugeshp at English Wikipedia. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Abanindranath Tagore
people.summary: Founder of the Bengal School of painting; his "Bharat Mata" (1905) became an icon of the Swadeshi movement.
facts: Founder of the Bengal School of painting; his "Bharat Mata" (1905) became an icon of the Swadeshi movement.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
